cards.text: We're in Egypt now, friend. The people of Judah went down there even though the LORD told them to stay home (Jeremiah 43:4-7), and they've spread out to Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and Pathros. Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah the prophet about every one of them.
The LORD of Hosts opens with something they've all seen with their own eyes: Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, lying in ruins today. No slideshow needed, because they just LEFT it.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Jerusalem and the cities of Judah are lying in ruins?

answers.text: Because of the evil they had done
Because their walls were built too weak
Because their army was far too small

cards.question: The LORD says the other gods Judah burned incense to were gods their fathers had always known.

cards.text: And this didn't come out of nowhere. God sent His servants the prophets again and again with His message: 'Do not do this detestable thing that I hate.'

cards.question: When the prophets kept warning them, the people of Judah stopped burning incense to other gods.
Since Judah would not listen to the prophets, the LORD says His ___ poured out on the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to the people right there in Egypt with a question. Why are they doing such great harm to themselves, cutting off man and woman, child and infant from Judah, until there's no remnant left?

cards.question: The LORD asks why the people are provoking Him by burning incense to other gods in Egypt. What does He say they will become among all the nations?

answers.text: An object of cursing and reproach
Servants to the king of Egypt

cards.text: Then God asks them straight out: have they forgotten? The wickedness of their fathers, of the kings of Judah and their wives, and their OWN wickedness back in the streets of Jerusalem.

cards.question: The LORD says that to this day the people have humbled themselves.

cards.text: So the LORD says He will set His face to bring disaster and cut off all Judah. That includes the remnant who resolved to go to Egypt and live there.

cards.question: From the least to the greatest, how does the LORD say the remnant who went to Egypt will die?
The LORD says He will punish those living in Egypt just as He punished Jerusalem.

cards.text: Here's the part that stings. These people long to go back to Judah and live there again.

cards.question: Who does the LORD say will make it back from Egypt to Judah?

cards.text: Now the people answer Jeremiah, and this isn't two guys grumbling in the back row, it's a GREAT assembly. The men who knew their wives were burning incense to other gods are there, with the women standing by and the people living in Egypt and Pathros.

cards.question: What does the great assembly tell Jeremiah about the word he spoke in the name of the LORD?

answers.text: We will not listen to you
We will do all you say

cards.text: Then they say what they WILL do: everything they vowed, burning incense to the Queen of Heaven, one of those other gods, and pouring out drink offerings to her, just like their fathers, their kings and their officials did back in Judah. Wrong direction, full commitment.

cards.question: Back when they burned incense to the Queen of Heaven in Judah, what do the people say life was like?

answers.text: Plenty of food and no disaster

cards.question: The people say that since they stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven, they have lacked everything.

cards.text: Then the women speak up: they burned incense to the Queen of Heaven, poured out drink offerings and made sacrificial cakes in her image. And they ask Jeremiah if any of that happened without their husbands' knowledge.
Now Jeremiah answers all of them, men and women. He brings up all that incense burned in Judah's cities and Jerusalem's streets, by them, their fathers, their kings, their officials, everybody.

cards.question: Jeremiah asks the people: did the LORD not ___ all that incense burned in Judah and Jerusalem?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah points to their land: it became a desolation, a horror and an object of cursing, without inhabitant, still that way today.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the disaster came on them because they stopped serving the Queen of Heaven.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah brings one more word from the LORD. The LORD repeats their own vow to the Queen of Heaven back to them and says, 'Go ahead, then, do what you have promised! Keep your vows!'

cards.question: The LORD swears an oath. What does He say the men of Judah living in Egypt will never again do?
The LORD says He is watching over the men of Judah in Egypt for good and not for harm.

cards.text: A few who escape the sword will return from Egypt to Judah. And the whole remnant will find out who had it right all along.

cards.question: The whole remnant of Judah in Egypt will know whose ___ will stand: the LORD's or theirs.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives them a sign that He will punish them in this place, so they'll know His threats will surely stand. And He has a word about Pharaoh Hophra, king of the very land they moved to.

cards.question: What does the LORD say will happen to Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt?

answers.text: He will be handed to his enemies
He will send Judah back home

cards.text: The LORD says it'll go just like it did for Zedekiah, king of Judah, whom He delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. The king they ran to for safety? Same story.
